channel.title: wuld.ink — changelog
channel.description: Changes to wuld.ink — for posterity and transparency.

item.title: The default ambience is calmer now: the YouTube background player no longer starts on its own — turn it on from the bar if you want it — and the generative synth bed carries the room by default, opening on breeze: a deep, methodic drone with an aching resonant wind that rises and aches back between movements, after the opening of Éliane Radigue's Triptych. Two other moods sit a tap away in the [fx] panel — a colder clinical hum and a deeper oceanic drift tuned to carry on smaller speakers.

Two other moods sit a tap away in the [fx] panel — a colder clinical hum and a deeper oceanic drift tuned to carry on smaller speakers.

item.title: New Notes tab — a private place to write, saved only in your browser (nothing is sent anywhere unless you copy or download it). Typing has sound and a soft glow, and each finished word lands with a chime. The ambient layer grew too: the site quietly drifts and glitches the longer you leave a tab open, and the generative synth bed gained two new moods — a colder clinical hum and a deeper oceanic drift — cycled from the [fx] panel.

item.title: New help page for a connection error some visitors hit — an intermittent ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR or “invalid response” warning that comes and goes. It’s a network-side Encrypted ClientHello (ECH) conflict, not the site: /troubleshooting/ has the roughly 30-second fix, by browser, with a mirror on library.wuld.ink for when the main domain won’t load. Linked from the footer and the contact page.

item.title: The flagship library now has plain language too. That completes the rollout: every library surface — the flagship and all five wings — now offers a plain-language reading.

item.title: A new wing joins the Refusal Libraries: Anthropocentrism. It answers the objections raised when human moral priority is questioned — from 'humans are simply the rational default' through species-membership and substrate to the charge that any such dissent is mere misanthropy. Six objections, provisionally complete, each graded, with real-world examples cited. It defends the permissibility of declining the anthropocentric mandate and asserts no positive ranking of its own; reach it from the wing-switcher at the top of any library page.

item.title: You can now save plates. A star in the corner of every plate bookmarks it to a Saved list that persists in your browser, and the controls bar gains a Saved toggle that filters to just those — on any page, and across every room from the lobby. Search now understands plate numbers: type 1, 001, or plate 001 to pull up every plate numbered one, across rooms (the Roman-numbered editorial plates included), instead of matching id fragments. And the lightbox gains a randomizer — a [ random ] button beside the arrows, or press r — to jump to a random plate. Flagged plates stay withheld behind the consent gate throughout; starring is by id, so it works before you reveal anything.

item.title: Library v3.9.11 — legible-mode review-note legibility (maintenance). The dependency graph's per-premise review notes were pinned at 10px and sat outside the legible set, so switching to legible re-fonted them to serif while keeping the 10px box — they read smaller than standard. Legible and legible+high-contrast now render the notes at 12.5px with relaxed leading on both the combined and index surfaces; standard and high-contrast are unchanged, and the note badges keep their small label size by design. Render-only CSS; canon held at v37.36 per the Exchange-38 ruling.

item.title: Library v3.9.10 — dependency-panel review-note riders (maintenance). The dependency graph's per-premise review notes — short audit annotations shown when a premise node is clicked — still quoted connection totals from the v3.5 audit, when the graph was smaller. Five premise notes read as if those counts were current: Consent Impossibility (62 total connections), Suffering as Deterrence (13), Contextus Claudit (8), Alogical Isness (8), Convergent Architecture (13). Each figure now carries a small inline rider giving the live count beside the audit figure — current: 67 (42 strong / 25 weak), 19, 9, 11, and 17 respectively. The v3.5 audit text itself is unchanged: the old figures stay as clearly dated history rather than being rewritten, the same convention v3.9.9 applied to the graph's explanatory note. The fourteen objection-level notes needed nothing — their counts still match the live graph. No rebuttal, score, edge, or graph data changed; the dependency graph still holds its locked 254 edges.

The note now reports the current graph: Consent Impossibility sources 67 edges, 42 strong and 25 weak, which is 26% of the 254 dependencies the graph actually holds. The note now reports the current graph: Consent Impossibility sources 67 edges, 42 strong and 25 weak, which is 26% of the 254 dependencies the graph actually holds. The older v3.5 audit figures are kept but clearly marked as history rather than read as current. No rebuttal, score, edge, or graph geometry changed — only the wording of the note; the dependency graph still holds its locked 254 edges. Version and provenance continue to live in the changelog and the integrity pin, not in the note. (Sections: /argument-library/)

item.title: Library v3.9.8 — panel corrections (maintenance). Three small text fixes to the library's explanatory panels, with no change to any rebuttal, score, or graph geometry. The dependency-graph notes no longer claim Autonomy is the system's most common weakness — a stale line that contradicted the methodology panel, which correctly identifies Robustness — and the Autonomy note now describes what the graph actually shows: which responses lean on contested foundational premises and so persuade a determined skeptic least. The masthead drops its version number, which had drifted out of date; the live version lives in the changelog and the integrity pin, not the title. And the list of highest-scoring entries now reads 'include' rather than 'are', since the four named entries are examples drawn from a larger set of ten that score top marks on all five axes, not the whole set.

item.title: Library v3.9.7 — methodology-panel reconcile (correctness). The RSI methodology panel now states its own grading conventions in full: grades band the unrounded geometric mean while displayed percentages round to one decimal — so a boundary cell can legitimately read 88.0/B — and a worked example (privileged-first-world, long form) carries the arithmetic end-to-end from five axis scores to the final letter. The panel's fourth axis label normalizes from Resilience to Robustness (label only; no score changes), and a stale calibration claim that Autonomy was the library's most common weakness is replaced with the ledger-true observation that Robustness is. The five axis names and definitions are now canonized exactly as the deployed panel defines them — the definitions the 81 stored scores were actually assigned against. Reading modes pick up the panel correctly. No rebuttal text, scores, or graph geometry change.

item.title: Library v3.9.6 — dependency-graph de-clutter (maintenance). The dependency graph's objection band now lays out as five tier-keyed columns instead of one crowded strip: each objection sits in its tier's column, dense tiers stagger their entries around the column line with spacing sized to each node, and the heaviest premise hubs hold their dependents at distance instead of knotting them into a clump. Reading modes that narrow the page to a comfortable prose measure no longer narrow the graphs with it — all three graph views keep the full frame while prose pages keep their measure. Geometry only; graph data and the reading modes themselves are untouched.

item.title: Library v3.9.5 — graph-view legibility (maintenance). The display toggle's LEGIBLE and BOTH modes now apply a typographic treatment inside the three graph views instead of only repainting the theme: node labels step up in size and weight behind a semi-opaque halo-chip, so they read against dense linework without enlarging the graph itself, and the side panels and methodology panels ride the same legibility scale. Graph tabs default to STANDARD on entry — the layout-optimal view — and restore your prior reading mode on leave; an explicit mode choice made inside a graph sticks. Graph geometry, data, and zoom are untouched.

item.title: Library v3.9.4 — band-convention correction. RSI letter grades return to banding the unrounded geometric mean (the ratified v37.13 convention), reverting a drift that had promoted ten boundary-edge long-form rebuttals to A and softened two mediums. Headline distribution moves to A26/B54/C1 — the principled outcome, not a regression. Displayed percentages keep one-decimal rounding, so a boundary cell can legitimately read 88.0/B: the precise value sits just under the line.
